name: Branch Manager
label: Dischord
lede: Branch Manager came out of Reston, Virginia, made two albums for Dischord, got Ian MacKaye to help mix the second, and broke up in December 1997 after a tour that went badly enough for the label to mention it.

eras.title: Big in Reston
eras.text: Reston is a planned community about 20 miles west of Washington. Dischord says the trio made a name there first, then started to register in DC, and that "those who saw them swore by them."

years.h: Reston gets a trio: Branch Manager
years.p: [[Ron Winters|0829b0f9-1629-4099-9602-353940c33422]] on guitar and lead vocals, [[Dave Allen|f0f0d560-560b-4d40-883e-b795105446d0]] on bass and vocals, [[Derrick Decker|34dc89bf-5466-4563-a404-1599f96adbff]] on drums. AllMusic dates the start to 1990.
years.xp:
Reston was built in the 1960s as a model suburb, a long way in spirit from the DC punk houses. Dischord's history says the band built a name at home before it started to register in the city.

AllMusic hears [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] in them, with a wider range of influences than most of their label mates. A fan-posted tape, labeled as their first show, is dated January 6, 1991 at DC Space.

years.h: Branch Manager's first show, DC Space, January 6, 1991
yt: Branch Manager's first show, DC Space, January 6, 1991

years.h: Two singles on VHF and Level come first
years.p: Branch Manager put out singles on VHF Records and Level Records before Dischord signed them.

eras.title: Onto the Dischord train
eras.text: The self-titled debut put a suburban trio on the same label as Fugazi and Jawbox. AllMusic says they sounded like neither, which helped and hurt.

years.h: Dischord No. 95 is Branch Manager's self-titled debut
years.p: Eleven songs, from "Bent Flagpole" to "Unemployed Ninja" to "Hate, Resentment, And Jealousy." The band's Bandcamp dates it September 1, 1995.
years.xp: Dischord says the band toured a lot and played several dates with Fugazi. "Floored and to the Left" is one of the album's tracks.

years.h: Dischord band, AllMusic says, and that was the catch
years.p: AllMusic's verdict: the label and the locale probably kept them from being known as more than another Dischord band.

eras.title: Tribal, then tired
eras.text: Ian MacKaye helped mix the second album. A rough trip later in 1997 finished the band, and it disbanded in December.

years.h: Anything Tribal, Dischord No. 107, opens with "Irrationally Yours"
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear Studios and mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band. Nine songs, including "The Guacamole Act of 1917" and "Nathan's Pets & Auto Supplies."
years.xp: The title track and "The Holly Syndrome" sit alongside "Frozen Sneakers, IN." on the nine-song tracklist. Dischord's store lists it on CD and as a download.

years.h: A grueling trip in 1997, and the band is gone by December
years.p: Dischord says Branch Manager cracked up after a particularly grueling trip and disappeared from sight, two albums and seven years in.
years.xp: Dischord doesn't say where the trip went or what happened on it, and no interview on the record fills it in.

eras.title: Afterward
eras.text: Branch Manager have a place on Dischord's 20th-anniversary compilation, and Ron Winters kept playing.

years.h: 20 Years of Dischord includes the band
years.p: The label's anniversary compilation, Dischord No. 125, carries Branch Manager.

years.h: Winters is back in 2007 with Sons of Disobedience
years.p: His later band puts out a four-song EP in April, per Dischord.
